Hi [~accountid:63fe21787c30bbd6b33e09d3] - could you please provide a bit more context around why you have concluded that Section 15(1) requires Bolt to provide this information? I am not sure I agree with this based on the following analysis:

*LEGAL BASIS ANALYSIS*

* [Regulation 7 of the Child Support Information Regulations 2008:|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2008/2551/contents]
** This Reg says that “_persons required_” to furnish information must do so. ‘Persons required’ are listed in Regulations 3 to 6, and include:
*** The applicant (which does not apply to Bolt)
*** The non-resident parent (which does not apply to Bolt)
*** A person for whom the non-resident parent is providing or has provided services under a contract for services (I understand that Luke Field is a rider rather than a driver based on the ticket description - but +*we should check this*+. If Luke is a rider, this would not apply).
*** A person that denies parentage (which does not apply to Bolt)
*** A court (which does not apply to Bolt)
** As such, if Luke is a rider, I do not see how Bolt is a person that is required to provide information to the CMS here. Indeed, the letter says that Bolt “may” have been under a duty to provide this information, which makes our obligations here unclear.
* [+Section 15(4) of the Child Support Act 1991+|https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1991/48/section/15/enacted]:
** This says that an inspector can enter Bolt’s premises “_to make such examination and enquiry there as he considers appropriate_”. 
** I am reading this provision in the context of Section 14: “_The Secretary of State may make regulations requiring any information or evidence needed for the determination of any application under this Act_”, which seems to be directly linked to the CSIR 2008 (see above).
** My reading of this (let me know if you disagree) is therefore that an inspector can enter premises to ask for information that they are entitled to demand under Regulation 7 (which currently I am not sure they can do in this case).
* I am therefore not convinced that Bolt is *_required_*  to provide this information to the CMS, unless we find out that Luke Field is a driver.

If we end up concluding that we are not _legally required_ to provide this information, then the key question becomes whether we can otherwise afford to share this information based on Bolt’s own legitimate interests. A core element of this analysis is whether the request from the CMS is *proportionate* (as we should not be over-sharing data) - IMO, we have not been provided with enough context to assess this point. The CMS has given next to no context on what they are investigating, nor why the data they are requesting is necessary for this investigation, and so I would be minded to push the CMS for more details before we respond.

*In short, I think we should:*

# Check whether Luke Field is indeed a rider, rather than a driver, with Bolt.
# Write back to the CMS and:
## Push them on the legal basis point (i.e., their letter says Bolt “_may_” have been under a duty to provide the requested information. We want them to confirm whether Bolt +is+ under this duty).
## Push them for more context on why they need the requested information (we can leverage wording from our standard response to stress: (1) we are committed to cooperating with these kinds of requests; but (2) we need to make sure we have a proper legal basis, and without additional context we cannot assess whether the grounds being cited actually apply; and (3) it is difficult to determine whether we are complying with data minimisation unless we know what the data will be used for).
# Once CMS respond, if we have enough confirmations on legal basis / purpose, we can then respond.

The information in the article Escalation Guidelines is not easily accessible, it would not easily come to an agent’s mind to check that article when handling an overcharge case for example (why would they think to check the Escalation Guidelines if in the relevant KB it says the case is handled by Tier 1), we need to have it as visible as possible, especially since agents from other markets are regularly assigned to assist us with tickets, given the current regulatory situation in Romania, we cannot afford to miss any Consumer Protection threat.

The Tier 2 agents check if the response sent by Tier 1 agents was ok, if the case was handled correctly, if mistakes were made, Tier 2 agents will make sure the case is handled correctly moving forward. If the case was handled correctly according to the process, but the user is still unhappy, the Tier 2 agents will issue a refund as a one time exception (if it’s the first time the user has threatened to raise a consumer protection complaint). The steps for Tier 2 agents don’t need to be documented since we already know what to do, the issue is with T1 agents, especially those being assigned from other markets to help with backlog.

Hi [~accountid:632ac798b2e3c5ad0fa1dd3e] , I have a couple of questions before I finalize the privacy assessment. In short, this isn’t a no-go, but we need to document and assess the feature to spot any risks (which I don’t expect there to be).

# *Countries where we’ll launch this*

You mentioned that we won’t be launching this globally to avoid overlaps with the Family Accounts Feature. Do we have a list of countries where we want to launch this?

# *Data storage and retention*

The RFC mentions that there will be a possibility to order a trip for a a saved rider that the account user has added previously. Where will this information be stored and for how long? Is it possible to remove it, in case the person taking the trip asks CS to do so? For context, we’re receiving such requests for the Trusted Contact feature, so I want to see if it’ll be possible with this feature.

# *Types of data collected*

Am I correct that we’ll only be collecting this information:

* Name of the person taking the trip (added by the person booking the trip)
* Phone number of the person taking the trip (added by the person booking the trip)
* Pick up point and drop-off point of the person taking the trip

Are we going to collect anything else, such as geolocation data, payment data, etc?

# *Drivers contacting the person taking the trip*

As far as I know, in all countries we have either phone masking or VoIP. Does this mean that the driver will never see the number of the person taking the trip? Or will they see the account owner’s number?

A lot of lost item cases are escalated to the CS in case the rider can’t contact the driver anymore. I suggest having this in mind / liaising with the CS team on how the process should look like from a CS POV.

In principle however, it is already regulated in the TCs - pursuant to clause 7.2. “_A party may terminate the Agreement at any time and for any reason by notifying the other party at least 7 days in advance_” and the rules for delivery of any notices are specified in clause 8.1. So naturally the notice period starts upon delivery of termination notice whereas the moment of delivery is specified in clause 8.1. 

Please clarify what is expected - does the client want to exclude possibility to provide termination notice via e-mail / Business portal and keep only registered letter or courier?

** Conducting registration checks upon registration on the Bolt platform only on a selected basis.

+*BACKGROUND*+

* Feature concerns way-finding. 
** In the next two months, we will be including routes in the app re how passengers can reach a pick-up point. These routes will contain a step-by-step guide, as well as photos.
** Current requests concern Poland only. However, it seems we have previous UK examples ([here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-29502] and [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-30467]).
* Request is whether there are any restrictions on what Bolt can put in such photos.
** This question is mainly framed in the terms of whether we can include corporate logos. However, there are Privacy elements - aim is that we will blur the faces of any people in the photos.

+*PRIVACY ANALYSIS*+

* Best outcome would be for us to not process any personal data, which would remove the privacy risks.
** Only personal data here would be people in the photos, number plates, residential addresses.
*  As such, the clear solution seems to be to ensure these are always blurred.
** Otherwise, we would get into all sorts of issues re processing third-party data.

+*QUESTIONS*+

* Will we be limiting this to certain locations (e.g., airports)?
* Who is taking the photos in the first place?

Currently:
_Campaign valid for companies who sign up for a Business account dd.mm.yyyy or later. Discount valid until dd.mm.yyyy for a period of three months following its application and only for On-demand Rides in the country of application. Maximum total discount €50._

Suggested:
_For new business accounts. Max discount applies. T&Cs apply._

*Recommendation:*
If the issue is reflecting the market specific currency then I suggest to use a formulation where the exact currency is reflected in an open-ended way, e.g. _Maximum total discount €50_ *_or equivalent_*_._ 

If we just use _Maximum total discount is limited/ applies_ or similar w/o providing the value itself then it’s of very little value in a dispute. Comprehensive campaign terms should be shared before the customer signs up and applies the code. 

If the recommendation cannot be followed for operational/commercial purposes then this is a risk which requires a business/risk decision. 

*Question:*

The wording you suggested goes beyond the currency issue. Please let me know if there are further elements you’d like to change in the wording of the creative based on what has been discussed earlier in this ticket.

Additionally, we carefully assess each law enforcement request to ensure only the minimal amount of data required for the specified purpose is disclosed.

Okay, so I’m re-defining this issue a bit: 

Reports are increasing again that support teams are struggling to assist drivers who some reason cannot do an early cashout. As they define this is a problem with early cashout and there is no other available information (than trip count) for support to consider, these cases tend to reach the partner payments team who in turn either send them to us or use their operational resource to inform the support agents. 

In order to avoid overloading partner payments with decision cases coming from our end, it would make sense for us to cut off unnecessary escalations altogether. Early cashouts are a benefit, a feature - meaning really we don’t need to get escalations for individual cases - the drivers have an opportunity to receive their funds the regular weekly way as a fallback and/or can try again on the next times. 

So how I see it is that the problem really is not that the cases reach partner payments BUT rather that they are escalated due to insufficient visibility on our end to ‘exclude’ issues that may be on fraud side. Hypothesis is that if we were to add a visibility on fraud side to say “yes, fraud said reject” then we’d remove the unnecessary cases AS WELL AS can make our own conditions for further escalations to come to the right place.

Thanks [~accountid:5f1a8e14e5efc1001bf8ec6d] for the clarification , all clear. I believe the delivery service invoice is correct by not showing that extra line, since fiscalization rules apply and may not allow for that (i.e. the campaign it is not shown - as it stands at present in PT).

Coming back to [~accountid:627cd41af29dcb0068f9650a], your query is very valid, but we do not have a satisfactory answer. In line of what Helena already explained:

A) *For the Food order*, it is the Merchant the party obliged to provide the Eater with a legally valid receipt/invoice. Bolt is not the party selling the goods, thus it is not responsible for issuing and providing it. Nonetheless Bolt does issue an informative Cost Summary to the Eater, available upon request (see the one attached by Juan). Whenever we have a Campaign (not a discount. A discount could only be provided by the good´s seller, the Merchant), it should be understood as a marketing campaign cost that Bolt decides to bear, and reduces the cost after taxes (VAT) of the whole order. Indeed, since the POS of the merchant and Bolt system are not synchronized, there is no way that the Merchant can capture such Campaign provided by Bolt on the legal receipt expeded from Merchant > Eater. *Conclusion:* 1) The only source doc matching the payment would be the informative Cost Summary, unfortunately, which is not a legally valid tax receipt/invoice, and 2) The Merchant would still receive, as per your example, EUR 8 from the Eater, plus EUR 2 from Bolt, thus being able to correctly declare revenue and VAT on the full amount of the sale.

B ) *For the Delivery service*, in this case Bolt is issuing the legally valid receipt on behalf of the Delivery Partner, which is the party rendering the service to the Eater. Again, since the Delivery Partner is not providing any discount, but rather it is Bolt the party running a marketing campaign to decrease the cost after taxes of the service, this is not reflected in the fiscalised invoice for delivery, so there is still a mismatch between the amount that was paid and what the doc reflects. In other countries, where there are not fiscalisation rules, we have recently included an extra line at the bottom of the invoice, where it is shown what was the total amount after Campaign paid by the Eater (“charged to Client”). This is not the case in Portugal, thus the mismatch you mention remains.

What we should do is have the following rule:

* agents don’t disclose their name by default. 
* If pushed by the police, agents let them know that this is Bolt (the company) who is disclosing the data and handling the request, and therefore the name of the agent is irrelevant, as the agent is only acting as the POC for reacting to the request, and not handling it. 
* only if the police further pushes the agent to disclose their name, the agent can tell their full name but is not required to disclose their full name and explains the situation as described in the bullet point above. 

​The arguments for such pushback is:

* Bolt adheres to strict requirements under privacy laws which require the company to share only the data that is necessary, and to ensure that it is minimized to the extent possible. 
* The person who is answering their call (agent) is not necessarily the person who will be handling their request. Bolt has robust internal policies and procedures, which ensure that the requests are reviewed and approved by relevant responsible employees.

I do not agree with JinShun. Their datasheet lacks information or even if it does not then it is possible to misinterpret their datasheet.

In their specification, 36V is marked as “rated voltage” - This to me means that this is the voltage at which the motor is supposed to be the most efficient, however:

* There is no mention what is the highest or lowest voltage that is allowed to be used. The motor coil voltage depends on the modulated voltage by the controller, it is not directly related to the battery voltage.
* JinShun specification sheet indicates, that the “Maximum torque” is 22Nm IN CASE the current is limited to 15A.
** The JinShun datasheet specifies “Maximum torque”, it does not specify maximum current.
** This is what JinShun datasheet says:
!image-20250225-124154.png|width=441,height=75,alt="image-20250225-124154.png"!

** Even if the JinShun datasheet is interpreted in a way that “15A” Is the “maximum allowed current” then the datasheet still lacks important constraints - A time or temperature should be specified how long such current is allowed to be used.

* JinShun datasheet does not directly provide maximum power which they claim to be 540W.
** Even if the “maximum power” allowed is 540W, there are no constraints set in place that how long such power is allowed to be supplied to the motor.

I think that Bolt and Jinshun have different understanding of the specification that they have provided. I think that this argument can go on forever from both sides. In my opinion we should find a solution instead and help JinShun improve their specsheets if they want to use our help. This could help to prevent such events to happen in the future.

# *Could you please confirm whether Bolt will receive the insights derived by Braze's AI algorithms* *_before_* *messages are sent to users?*

Answer: 

_No, recommendations will be created and inserted to emails/pushes automatically. And Bolt won’t get any notifications or reports with recommendations created for all users, before they will be sent._ 

_At the same time, Bolt determines which providers / dishes can or cannot be recommended. It’ll be managed by CSV file uploaded to Braze. Recommendations will consist only from the providers / dishes from the uploaded file. If the provider won’t be in that file, it won’t be recommended to users._

_Also, it’s possible to check recommendations created to each user manually before we send communication (but it can be done only by checking each users' recommendations one be one)._

# *Will Braze make the* *_final_* *decision on which personalized communication to send to each user, or will Bolt retain control over this decision?*

Answer: 

_Braze will create and insert recommendations to emails/pushes automatically. We don’t consider to have any process for double-checking the created recommendations in a bulk. At the same time, before sending communication, we’ll double check created recommendations manually for a small segment of users. Also, we’ll be able to prevent some users from getting the comms with recommendations created by Braze._

# *To confirm, regarding location data, only the IP address is used, and from the IP address, the country and city are derived. Is this correct?*

Answer: 

_We don’t pass users' IPs to Braze. At the same time we pass users' city and country – and they’ll be used for recommendations._

# *In the "Which personal data will be used in the project" section in the DPIA, the following data points were selected: i) contact data; ii) location data; iii) browsing data; iv) other categories of non-sensitive personal data; and v) digital behavior. However, in the "Please explain the answer given in the previous question" section, only the following data points are described: i) contact data; ii) location data; and iii) information about purchases.  Could you please clarify whether "information about purchases" includes browsing data, other categories of non-sensitive personal data, and digital behavior?*

We won’t use any external information about users' purchases, their browsing history or any other digital behaviour. What will be used – information about purchases made inside Bolt Food app.

Hi [~accountid:603fcbd5333ff40070e0e343] for Newport:

The Addendum states that we had an agreement from 2022. Now we're adding another company to that agreement, so both companies are responsible for following it. This new paper, plus the old agreement, is now the final word on our arrangement.

Here is each point explained: 

* *"Addendum to License Agreement"*: This is another way of saying "an extra piece of paper that changes our original agreement."
* *"Made as of [24/02/2025]"*: This tells us when this change becomes official. Will reflect the date that we sign.
* *"Rombourne Limited (the 'Licensor')" and "Bolt Services UK Limited (the 'Licensee')"*: These are the names of the companies involved, with their addresses and company numbers. "Licensor" is the one giving permission, and "Licensee" is the one receiving it.
* *"WHEREAS, the Licensor and Licensee entered into a License Agreement dated 10 February 2022 (the 'Agreement')"*: This reminds everyone that they already have a previous agreement in place.
* *"WHEREAS, the parties desire to amend the Agreement..."*: This means they both agree to change the original agreement.
* *"NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements..."*: This basically says, "Because we both agree to this, here's what we're changing."
* *"1. Amendments"*: This section explains the actual changes.
** *"1.1. The Licensee definition...shall include..."*: This is the key change. It's saying that now, _two_ companies are considered "Licensees" (the ones getting permission):
*** The original company, Bolt Services UK Limited.
*** A new company, Bolt Operations UK Limited.
** *"1.2. The Licensees shall be jointly and severally liable."*: This means that both companies are responsible for following the agreement, and if one of them messes up, the other one is also responsible.
* *"2. Entire Agreement"*: This confirms that this new document, along with the original agreement, is the complete and final understanding between the companies. Nothing else matters.

Hopefully this helps.

Thanks all - I appreciate that there is a call scheduled for tomorrow to discuss the status on this one, given that we are aiming for roll-out by the end of the month. As such, below are my thoughts on this from the Privacy side (see both the summary and more detailed advice).

{panel:bgColor=#e3fcef}
*In short:*

We are ok with *green-lighting* this feature, *_provided that_*:

* We are keeping a *paper trail* of why a particular document was accepted;
* The automated process does not significantly increase the chance of *fraudulent documents* being accepted;
* We are providing drivers with a high-level *explanation of why a document is rejected* (if we are not already doing so); and
* I can +_first_+ get some {color:#ff5630}*more clarification on the extent to which ChatGPT / other third-party tools will be used*{color} as part of the automated acceptance process.
{panel}

*MORE DETAILED ADVICE*

This feature is not directly related to the ICO investigation, incorporates human review in cases of document rejection, and I understand that we are not for now doing any biometric processing / reviewing criminal or medical documents. These all  significantly lower the risk profile.
Our main concerns with the feature are as follows:
*(1) Transparency*
There are some updates that will be needed to the driver privacy notice to reflect these newly automated processes, but we can incorporate these as part of the global process for updating the notices. In any event, they should not act as a blocker.
Otherwise, we also want to ensure sufficient transparency for drivers regarding the reason(s) why a document was rejected. I appreciate that we are incorporating human review in the rejections process which is great to hear, but drivers may still complain about any rejections and ask for further information. If we are not doing so already, we should ensure that where a driver is rejected, they are provided with a high-level explanation as to why.
*(2) Accepting fraudulent documents*
This feature sounds like a good idea from an operational perspective. The main practical issue I can foresee, however, is that by automating the document acceptance process, there is a risk that certain fraudulent documents may slip through the net and be automatically accepted. If the driver whose fraudulent documents were accepted is later the subject of an investigation, and the police / a regulator asked why they they were allowed on the platform, this would expose us to risk. As such, we are fine with using automated processes in this context, provided that they are robust and are very unlikely to allow fraudulent documents to slip through the cracks.
In any event, we should ensure that a clear paper trail is kept of all documents that are accepted, and why. Again, this is so that if we ever need to look into this for a specific driver, we will not encounter fact-finding issues or expose ourselves to unnecessary risk.
*(3) Third-party tools*
I have heard differing accounts on this SD ticket about whether ChatGPT is involved in this process at all. Before fully green-lighting this, we need this point confirmed, just so that we can be sure that appropriate security measures are in place.

Running EXPLAIN over problematic query:

{noformat} EXPLAIN SELECT du.id,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.created) as created,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.last_update) as last_update,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.start_processing_after) as start_processing_after,

FROM `document_unit` du
LEFT JOIN `document_item` di ON (du.id = di.unit_id)    
WHERE du.external_entity_type = 'driver'
    AND du.external_entity_id = 5659515
    AND du.requested_veritas_document_type = 'driving_license'
    AND di.status IN ('uploaded', 'pending_upload')
    AND di.document_type = 'py_driverslicense'
GROUP BY
    du.id
HAVING
    SUM(di.document_type='py_driverslicense') > 0
    AND (
        (MIN(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(di.created)) >= UNIX_TIMESTAMP(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - interval '1440' MINUTE) AND du.status = 'pending')
        OR (start_processing_after > UNIX_TIMESTAMP(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) AND du.status = 'queued')
    )
ORDER BY created ASC
LIMIT 1;{noformat}

||id||select_type||table||partitions||type||possible_keys||key||key_len||ref||rows||filtered||Extra||
|1|SIMPLE|di| |ALL|idx_unit_id_document_type| | | |2557098|4.0|Using where; Using temporary; Using filesort|
|1|SIMPLE|du| |eq_ref|PRIMARY,idx_created_status,idx_flow_run_uuid,idx_user_type_user_id_requested_veritas_document_type_status|PRIMARY|8|taxify_fleet_ocr.di.unit_id|1|5.0|Using where|

Looking initially at the report it looks that SQL does a full table scan over document unit and once document unit is found the join is performed and for document unit Index lookup is used, with eq_ref being a more precise (one-row) lookup.

Filtering by entity_type in document unit table I was expecting to heavy filter number of returned rows and later on perform the index lookup by unit_id in the document item table. 

Looking closer at the indexes we have in the document_unit table we have the index:

{noformat}  KEY `idx_user_type_user_id_requested_veritas_document_type_status` (`status`,`external_entity_id`,`external_entity_type`,`requested_veritas_document_type`) {noformat}

Judging by the name, it should be starting with sorting index initially by {{user_type}}after that by {{user_id}}, {{requested_veritas_document_type and status}} as we are having du.external_entity_type, du.external_entity_id in the WHERE clause, unfortunately if we take a look at the index definition and not name, the status is first column, due to this this index is not used. 

Ideally we just need an index on {{external_entity_id}}(using it, majority of records are dropped and we a left with just a couple of records). 

We have 2 options:

* Fix the index
* Add one extra condition to WHERE clause {{du.status IN ('pending', 'queued')}}, we are looking only to this statuses in the having clause.

Updated query using status filtering in WHERE:

{noformat}EXPLAIN
 SELECT du.id,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.created) as created,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.last_update) as last_update,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.start_processing_after) as start_processing_after,
    UNIX_TIMESTAMP(du.processed_at) as processed_at,
    du.status,
    du.is_renewal,
    du.requested_veritas_document_type,
    du.external_entity_type,
    du.external_entity_id,
    du.city_id,
    du.country,
    du.flow_run_uuid
FROM `document_unit` du
LEFT JOIN `document_item` di ON (du.id = di.unit_id)
WHERE du.external_entity_id = 5659515
	AND du.status IN ('processed' OR 'queued')
    AND du.external_entity_type = 'driver'
    AND du.requested_veritas_document_type = 'driving_license'
    AND di.status IN ('uploaded', 'pending_upload')
    AND di.document_type = 'py_driverslicense'
GROUP BY
    du.id
HAVING
    SUM(di.document_type='py_driverslicense') > 0
    AND (
        (MIN(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(di.created)) >= UNIX_TIMESTAMP(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - interval '1440' MINUTE) AND du.status = 'pending')
        OR (start_processing_after > UNIX_TIMESTAMP(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) AND du.status = 'queued')
    )
ORDER BY created ASC
LIMIT 1;{noformat}

We had a meeting with [~accountid:5c2c61f8d254b55db84ca612]  and decided to upgrade to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS along with a MySQL minor upgrade ref [https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/5.7/release-notes/release-notes_index.html|https://docs.percona.com/percona-server/5.7/release-notes/release-notes_index.html|smart-link] . Initially, we planned to upgrade the OS first, followed by MySQL, but this would introduce an unnecessary waiting queue for the MySQL upgrade. By performing both upgrades together and conducting performance testing using cluster mirroring, we can eliminate this delay while ensuring stability and identifying potential issues upfront.

The cluster-based mirroring tests have been successfully conducted and validated in previous MySQL → TiDB migrations, giving us confidence in this approach.

We chose Ubuntu 24 over Ubuntu 22 because Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (Noble Numbat) will be supported until 2034 under Ubuntu Pro, whereas Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (Jammy Jellyfish) reaches end-of-standard-support in 2027. Upgrading directly to Ubuntu 24 allows us to maximize the support window and avoid another OS upgrade in the near future. Additionally, Bolt SRE teams are already supporting Ubuntu 24.04, making this a logical follow-up step to align with the existing infrastructure and ensure consistency across the platform.

Sanny will compile an Architectural Decision Record (ADR) detailing the rationale, risks, and expected outcomes of this strategy. The ADR will be shared for review, and Sanny will present it at the upcoming TEX meeting to gather feedback.

Main issues across verticals:

* *Lack of assignment and notification features:* Multiple markets mentioned that Beehive lacks the ability to assign tasks to specific individuals and send notifications, which are crucial for efficient task management and collaboration
* *Not suitable for real-time communication and collaboration:* Slack is favored for its real-time communication and collaboration features, especially when multiple replies need to happen before the case can be solved. 
* *Lack of prioritisation in Beehive* - There’s a need for a *prioritisation* for tickets in BH, so that CS can mark high priority tickets, and escalate them to Local OPS
* *No way to request contact with user* - sometimes local OPS teams need CS to proactively reach out to users and there is no way other than Slack to request such contact to be made
* *No possibility to attach files in internal notes*

Delivery & Drive issues:

* Lack of Beehive access for certain teams:
** Delivery - OS teams who make menu adjustments
** Drive - Vehicle specialists (use tablets and tables are not compatible with Beehive) 

Drive specific issues:

* Cross-collaboration between teams and people on Beehive - some cases need multiple teams/team members involved to solve the case

*Reply (by Ragnar Rebase):*

The device_uid can be used as a supporting signal in combination with your other datapoints, not reliable on its own.

It's a uuid that is created for every "device" and persisted as long as the browser storage stays intact. Thus it's reset for the same user by

* clearing browser data/cache
* using private/incognito mode
* using different browsers



meaning:

* with this device_uid we can be sure that the connections it shows are true for the users (the exactly same device_UID token can not be created twice)
* however the related user list per one device_uid might not be comprehensive (due to clearing cache, incognito etc for some user sessions)
* however, it's currently possible that multiple users send the same device_uid if on the same device (browser) user logout -> login with different user (edited)

*1 - Privacy Notice*:

* While we initially [+advised+|https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-43252?focusedCommentId=2918153] that we will require a Privacy Notice for 3rd parties whose data we collect and share with MODA for KYC/AML purposes, we later understood and [+advised+|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C080SRRDB9B/p1738752656824639?thread_ts=1737729594.068889&cid=C080SRRDB9B] that: (i) we won't require consent from those parties; and (ii) we can rely on exception to avoid showing them a privacy notice.
* Essentially, this means that this task is now redundant and can be removed. Of course, we will still have our Driver and Passenger Privacy Notices ready for the funnel opening and launch and in those Notices, we will include a 'catch-all' consent and notice about KYC/AML data sharing, if we were ever required to disclose Driver and Passenger data with MODA.

*2 - Taiwan PDPA related regulations/guideline*:

* In our meeting with Baker McKenzie, they confirmed that the _Reference Guidelines for the Implementation of the Personal Data Protection Act in the Third-Party Payment Service Industry_ are merely non-binding guidelines and would be used as a point of reference by MODA if it were to audit Bolt. 
* As already mentioned, we have an existing Privacy compliance programme that addresses much of what MODA suggests in its Reference Guidelines. However, we have already begun a gap assessment for our own understanding and recording keeping to see whether there is anything major missing from our Internal privacy compliance programme. We are working with our Office of the Data Protection Officer (who manage this policies and procedures in this program) to finalise this gap assessment.
* If we identify any *major* gaps, we will work with Baker McKenzie to plug them.

* Deloitte will aggregate driver data from multiple platforms using hashed PHV license numbers. Since these hashes are consistent across platforms, they could be used to re-identify drivers. * Given the potential for re-identification, GDPR requires safeguards. A DSA will:
** Clearly define roles and responsibilities, minimizing liability risks.
** Limit data use to the agreed purpose, ensuring compliance.
** Enforce data security measures, preventing unauthorized access or re-identification.

Thank you. We checked with accounting partner, this is reply: 

Croatian General Tax Law and Value Added Tax Law contain provision that require provider of the services to issue invoice for the services performed. In addition, Article 157 of VAT Bylaw stipulates that one copy of the invoice is handed over to customer while the other is kept for accounting records of the taxable [person.In|http://person.In] addition, Croatian Fiscalisation Law in its Article 26 contains a provision that requires that all service recipients are required to keep invoice received until they leave the business premises of the service provider. Customers are also required to present the invoice to the CTA or Customs official when leaving the premises in the event of an audit.A fine in the range from 30 to 260 EUR is set for each customer that does not have the invoice when leaving the premisses or does not show it to CTA official if requested.So to conclude, there is an legal obligation to hand over the invoice to the customer.

h3. *Problem*

The problem occurs when we get *6-digit BINs* from Ethoca and try to [match them|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/03db41fd97be7d4df757fd6c2e881a6902c41133/src/platform/commerce/fraud_external_notification/main/table/PaymentDescriptorDataTable.ts#L34] with the rows in {{taxify_fraud_notification.payment_descriptor_data.}}

{{taxify_fraud_notification.payment_descriptor_data}} is filled by [Presto query|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/03db41fd97be7d4df757fd6c2e881a6902c41133/src/platform/commerce/fraud_external_notification/main/service/PaymentDataRetrievalServicePresto.ts#L24] from {{payment_payment_request_log}} table. The latter has *8-digit BINs*.

h3. *Solution*

*Ideal solution* would be to ask Ethoca to send us 8-digit BINs. That might mean the need to migrate to new API and can appear to be a bigger task. (*Estimate*: hard to estimate 😄)

*Quick-win solution* is to change [the query|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/03db41fd97be7d4df757fd6c2e881a6902c41133/src/platform/commerce/fraud_external_notification/main/table/PaymentDescriptorDataTable.ts#L34] to match by input card BIN *prefix*. This should work well since we already have the correct index on this table: {{(descriptor, card_bin, payment_id)}} (the last part is not being used currently). (*Estimate*: few hours)

The whole idea to manually update the durations is to:

# update the durations in Manual Review Block Requests (sadly the durations are inside the {{body_json}} field),
# update the durations in Blocks by setting “now” to those which should end if were 14-days blocks, and “start + 14 days” for those that should end in future.

There’s a CRON task that takes Blocks (only from the last 7 days) that should be finished and does whatever needed to unblock drivers.

Here are examples based on the Presto data:

Estimated number of Manual Review Block Requests to update:

{noformat}select count(block.id)
from glue.ng_public.manual_review_block_request block
where
  block.entity_type = 'driver'
  and (block.request_status = 'pending' or block.request_status = 'approved')
  and block.execution_result is null
  and block.body_json like '%"period":{"type":"duration","unit":"seconds","length":31536000}%'
  and block.body_json like '%\"duration_days\":365%'
  and block.reason_name = 'driver_contextual_block'{noformat}

*411*. They exist only for Driver Insights ({{driver_contextual_block}}), but don't exist for Driver Score ({{driver_behaviour_block_long_suspension}}).

Estimated number of Blocks to update:

{noformat}select count(block.id)
from glue.ng_public.block_block block
join glue.ng_public.block_reason reason on reason.id = block.reason_id 
where
  block.entity_type = 'driver'
  and block.status = 'active'
  and (reason.name = 'driver_contextual_block' or reason.name = 'driver_behaviour_block_long_suspension'){noformat}

*25582*. It's both for Driver Insights ({{driver_contextual_block}}) and Driver Score ({{driver_behaviour_block_long_suspension}}).

Body JSON content update preview:

{noformat}select replace(
  replace(
    block.body_json,
    '"period":{"type":"duration","unit":"seconds","length":31536000}',
    '"period":{"type":"duration","unit":"seconds","length":705600}'
  ),
  '\"duration_days\":365',
  '\"duration_days\":14'
)
from glue.ng_public.manual_review_block_request block
where
  block.entity_type = 'driver'
  and (block.request_status = 'pending' or block.request_status = 'approved')
  and block.execution_result is null
  and block.body_json like '%"period":{"type":"duration","unit":"seconds","length":31536000}%'
  and block.body_json like '%\"duration_days\":365%'
  and block.reason_name = 'driver_contextual_block'
limit 100{noformat}

End field update preview:

{noformat}select block.*, reason.name, case
  when timestamp '2025-02-27 10:00' > block.start + interval '14' day
    then timestamp '2025-02-27 10:00'
    else block.start + interval '14' day
  end
from glue.ng_public.block_block block
join glue.ng_public.block_reason reason on reason.id = block.reason_id 
where
  block.entity_type = 'driver'
  and block.status = 'active'
  and (reason.name = 'driver_contextual_block' or reason.name = 'driver_behaviour_block_long_suspension')
limit 100{noformat}

The challenge is that both users and authorities sometimes misunderstand our processes, assuming we are unwilling to assist, which leads to frustration. Additionally, when authorities reach out, their letters are often unclear or missing key compliance details, making it harder to process their requests efficiently.

To reduce back-and-forth and improve clarity, we propose creating a market-specific public article that outlines the correct process and provides an example of how an official request letter should be structured. This would help authorities and users understand exactly what is needed to get the required information, making the process smoother for everyone.

Based on what we had discussed, this solution will be implemented in multiple steps. 

* We will need to update the menu layout information we store in ES, because, if we are to set menu layout at ingestion, for the case we need to update the layout at menu ingestion, if the menu items number changes, and we already have a layout set, we will not longer know if that is a pre-set menu or it was an auto layout menu and we need to update accordingly to the new number of items. As such, we will update the data we store in ES per provider:


{noformat}export interface ProviderDocumentMenuMetadata extends ProviderDocumentMenuMetadataLight {
    id?: number | null;
    item_count?: number | null;
    variant_ids?: number[] | null;
    provider_defined_layout: DeliveryProviderInternalAsyncApi.MenuLayoutInEaterApp // add this value to keep track of the original layout values
}{noformat}



* Once we have the original values stored in ES, we can update the menu ingestion and provider ingestion logic as following:
** Menu ingestion logic:
*** Get menu data from provider index
*** If provider_defined_layout is auto → compute the menu layout based on the new number of items. Otherwise, keep the menu layout as it is
*** Update (if necessary) both ES and redis sources
** Provider ingestion logic:
*** If the received menu layout is not auto, update ES and redis sources with the new value
*** If the received menu layout is auto:
**** Either get the dish count from ES via menu index
**** Or get the dish count from provider index via menu data
**** Determine and save menu layout
** After we updated the ingestion logic, we can update the serving logic and just serve the menu layout as it is
*** We can also stop storing {{dish_count}} in Redis (as a bonus 🙂 )

*Background.* 
The Senior GM & the ops team with the Senior Ops Manager Trust & Safety LOPS as the POC, decided to review safety Ecs, etc in hopes of understanding the gaps in the market, mostly from a categorization standpoint. All Significant & High Events consequences seemed adequate. They thought certain Ecs under Low and Moderate should have a higher severity. 

My role was to explain the safety context and scenarios that would fit into these issues and triage the requests then present the final requests to Risk for review. 

1. The driver was smoking in the car during the ride - Smoking of marijuana like altering substances which I explained would fall under (Driver intoxication).
2. Rider Exposes Driver to Biological Factors - Pulled data (Rare report hence would have no impact)
3. Driver Speeding.  Speeding initiatives are already underway. 

*_Concerns for Low and Moderate/Reasons given:_*  
1. Blocking for low and moderate cases depends on grouping, allowing drivers to accumulate multiple offenses.
2. Too many soft blocks occur before a hard block is enforced. (Drivers in low-risk cases are given too many chances before being blocked, increasing the risk of serious offenses.)
3. The decay period for low and moderate offenses is too short.

We had a call, and I explained to them the concept of Demerit decay, counting precedence, and why exceptions cannot be made for these Just why they make sense as they are. 

*_Conclusion_* 
They settled on requesting an exception review for blocking for Low and moderate. 

*_Their POV was:_* 
1. Some drivers rarely read through educative or warning messages unless a block has been placed. 
2. Drivers are fully trained when joining the platform and are aware of appropriate conduct. 
3. Some of these low and moderate ECs are also tied to the country's laws hence the drivers already know this. 
4. To change the safety perspective, this is true for most african countries, drivers are the same across all platforms but only misbehave on the Bolt platform because in 5. Africa our competitors have stricter consequences for minor offenses. Drivers say “If I did that in Uber I would be blocked already”

Will update here the things we had to be dealing with during the migration to TiFlash

* [No index hints] In order for TiDB to decide to target TiFlash with the query, the query has to not contain any reference of index hints because those can be used only inside TiKV and TiDB will decide to not read some/all records from TiKV instead of TiFlash
* [Stale Table Stats in TiKv] Due to stale stats about the tables replicated in TiFlash, TiKV decided to execute the queries against TiKv instead - _a manual computation was triggered by DBAs here_
* [Filter & aggregation by enum values] Unfortunately TiFlash doesn’t have native support for {{enum}} aggregations and filtering ({{Warning | 1105 | Expression about 'taxify_delivery_order.order_courier.state' can not be pushed to TiFlash because it contains unsupported calculation of type 'enum'.}})
** Possible work around is to convert to varchar: {{CAST(o.state AS CHAR) AS o_state,}}
